repo_analysis_summary: LineIndex.build on improve/lineindex_build_throughput (1d2377e, src/indexer/lineIndex.ts L226-375) has the round-2 string loop (L266-291: 4x-unrolled 'buf[i..i+3] > 0x5c' reject at L267-274, then a byte tail) and the round-3 WCLS outer skip (L295-301). Best sealed score 1.623, target 1.8. Today the same file scores 1.605-1.680 in the sealed benchmark on this machine (i5-1340P, Node v24.21), so the recorded 1.623 sits at the low end of its noise band. Round 4's executor commit 360a642 (archive/round_4_executor_1) scored 1.590. ROOT CAUSE, now measured: 360a642 put the aligned Uint32Array word loop IN FRONT OF the existing 4x byte reject and kept that reject. The round-3/4 scratch candidate (g5.mjs strLoop 'swarU32') REPLACED the 4x reject. With the reject kept, i stops being 4-byte aligned right after any escaped pair or stop byte. The reject loop then moves i in steps of 4, so it stays misaligned, the ((base + i) & 3) === 0 gate fails, and the word loop barely runs. The only effect left is the cost of the extra gate. With the reject removed, the byte tail moves 1 byte per step (sb > 0x5c -> continue), so i is realigned within 3 bytes and the word loop takes over again. Isolation in round-5 scratch (C:/Users/chaowu21/AppData/Local/Temp/li-exp/r5 = TS copies of the branch file: base.ts = 1d2377e, exec4.ts = 360a642, plus variants made by exact string replacement in r5b/gen5*.mjs; r5b/bench-<v>.mjs = byte-identical copies of the sealed benchmark pointed at each variant; r5b/chk5.mjs = differential check against the sealed reference on edge fixtures plus unpooled buffers of every length mod 4, splits whole/1/2/7/64/1000, intervals 1024/1/3, async-iterable and string chunks, then 41 paired runs against base.ts in the same process). Sealed copies, alternating processes (sealed5b.log): base 1.643/1.643/1.680, swarR (word loop replaces reject) 1.895/1.882/1.865, swarK (scratch arithmetic: shifts, const view, but reject kept like 360a642) 1.607/1.615/1.617, exec4 1.631/1.631/1.610. swarK scores as low as exec4, so the per-chunk view allocation, '/ 4' vs '>> 2', Math.floor and 'let u32' are not the cause. Keeping the reject is. swarR as written THROWS 'Invalid typed array length' on an unpooled buffer whose last 1-3 bytes are unaligned (new Uint32Array(buf.buffer, aOff, 0) with aOff > byteLength). The sealed gate does not catch this because its fixtures sit on large pooled/concat buffers, but real reads can hit it. The guarded version swarRG passes all 576 differential cases and scores rel-vs-base 1.178 in-process (q1 0.960, q3 1.365) and sealed 1.837/1.871 against base 1.605/1.640 in the same sweep. A second family, quoteInline (scan the string body at the opening-quote case, with a one-time pre-loop carry block for strings that straddle a chunk start), is also positive: rel 1.159, sealed 1.787/1.790. Honest outlook: swarRG is the only single change measured at or above 1.8 in the sealed benchmark (5/5 runs at 1.837-1.895). Its expected value is about 1.62-1.68 x 1.13-1.15 = 1.83-1.90, which gives only about 2-5% of headroom over the target with ±4-8% run noise. A low run near 1.78-1.80 is plausible. Nothing else measured this round clears 1.8 alone.

ideas.title: swarRG: replace (not precede) the 4x byte reject with the aligned Uint32Array haszero word loop, with an empty-view guard
ideas.source: Round-5 isolation: r5/src/indexer/swarR.ts, swarK.ts, swarRG.ts (generated by r5b/gen5.mjs and gen5d.mjs from base.ts = 1d2377e); r5b/sealed5b.log; r5b/chk5.mjs. Compared against 360a642 (archive/round_4_executor_1) and round-4 scratch g5.mjs strLoop('swarU32'), which also has no rej4.
ideas.evidence: Sealed-benchmark copies, alternating processes: swarR 1.895/1.882/1.865 vs base 1.643/1.643/1.680 (sealed5b.log). swarRG 1.837/1.871 vs base 1.605/1.640 (sealed5c sweep). In-process paired vs base: rel median 1.178. Correctness: swarRG PASS 576 cases. swarR/swarK THROW on unpooled 5-10/4097-4099-byte buffers, so the guard is required. Control: swarK (same word loop and arithmetic, but rej4 kept after it, the 360a642 shape) 1.607/1.615/1.617, and exec4 1.631/1.631/1.610, both at or slightly below base. This shows the round-4 regression came from keeping the 4x reject (alignment lockout: rej4 advances by 4 from a misaligned i, so the word gate never re-fires), not from JIT effects, per-chunk allocation or '/4' arithmetic. EXACT single change on 1d2377e: (a) module level, next to WCLS: const EMPTY_U32 = new Uint32Array(0); (b) after 'const chunkBase = totalBytes;' (L255): const base = buf.byteOffset; const aOff = base + ((4 - (base & 3)) & 3); const wN = base + n > aOff ? (base + n - aOff) >>> 2 : 0; const u32 = wN > 0 ? new Uint32Array(buf.buffer, aOff, wN) : EMPTY_U32; (c) in the for(;;) at L266, DELETE the whole 'while (i + 3 < n && buf[i] > 0x5c && ... ) i += 4;' block (L267-274) and put in its place: if (((base + i) & 3) === 0) { let w = (base + i - aOff) >> 2; while (w < wN) { const x = u32[w]; const q = x ^ 0x22222222; const s = x ^ 0x5c5c5c5c; if (((((q - 0x01010101) & ~q) | ((s - 0x01010101) & ~s)) & 0x80808080) !== 0) break; w++; } i = aOff - base + (w << 2); } Keep the byte tail ('if (i >= n) break; const sb = buf[i++]; if (sb > 0x5c) continue; ...quote/backslash/escaped carry...') exactly as is. The planner and executor MUST NOT keep any 4x/rej4 loop, before or after the word loop: that is the exact 360a642 mistake. Correctness: the word loop stops on any word that has a 0x22 or 0x5c lane (haszero can also give false positives on lanes >= 0x80 after a borrow, which only send the word to the byte path), and the byte tail then handles it exactly as today. Not yet verified: repo vitest suites, tsc --noEmit and oxlint were not run on this variant, so the executor must run them.
ideas.estimated_impact: +13-15% relative (sealed ~1.83-1.90 from today's base 1.60-1.68; 5/5 sealed runs 1.837-1.895)

ideas.title: quoteInline: scan the string body at the opening-quote case instead of re-entering via the inString branch each outer iteration
ideas.source: r5/src/indexer/quoteInline.ts (generated by r5b/gen5c.mjs from base.ts); r5b/chk5.mjs; sealed copies bench-quoteInline.mjs
ideas.evidence: In-process paired vs base: rel median 1.159 (q1 0.994, q3 1.319). Sealed: 1.787/1.790 vs base 1.605/1.640 in the same sweep. PASS 576 differential cases, including chunk-straddling strings and a trailing backslash at a chunk end. Single change: remove the 'if (inString) { ... continue; }' branch at the top of the while loop (L258-293). Case 0x22 becomes: lineHasContent = true; i++; then the same rej4 + byte-tail for(;;) loop, which on i >= n sets inString = true and breaks, on a backslash at the last byte sets inString = true; escaped = true and breaks, and on the closing quote just breaks. Then 'continue'. Before 'while (i < n)', a one-time carry block runs only when the chunk starts inside a string: if (inString && n > 0) { if (escaped) { escaped = false; i = 1; } <same loop, setting inString = false on the closing quote and escaped = true on a backslash at the chunk end> }. The gain comes from dropping the per-outer-iteration inString test and the extra loop round-trip per string. It uses a different family from idea 1 and does not change the inner byte test. It probably will not reach 1.8 on its own (measured 1.787-1.790). Use it as the second-family plan or fallback, not as the primary bet. Stacking it with idea 1 (word loop inside the inlined scanner) is unmeasured and would be a separate later plan.

ideas.title: Later round only: stack the swarRG word loop inside the quoteInline scanner
ideas.source: Inference from ideas 1 and 2; not measured
ideas.evidence: Ideas 1 and 2 cut different costs: per-byte work inside strings vs per-string re-entry overhead. Both measured positive alone (1.178 and 1.159 rel). The combination was not built this round. Under H001 it is two changes, so it can only follow a merged idea 1 or idea 2. List it as an unmeasured lead for round 6. Do not plan it in round 5.

ideas.title: DO NOT: SWAR word loop placed in front of a kept 4x byte reject (360a642 / swarK shape), in any arithmetic form
ideas.evidence: exec4 sealed copies: 1.604/1.590/1.612 (sealed.log) and 1.631/1.631/1.610 (sealed5b.log) vs base 1.639/1.659/1.669 and 1.643/1.643/1.680. In-process rel 0.983. swarK (scratch arithmetic with shifts and a const view, rej4 kept) 1.607/1.615/1.617. Round 4's recorded 1.590 is the same result. Changing alignment checks, using Math.floor vs shifts, or hoisting the view cannot fix this shape, because the reject loop keeps i misaligned. Idea 1 is the corrected version.

ideas.title: NEUTRAL: hoist the escaped carry out of the string branch (strHoist)
ideas.evidence: escaped can only be true at i === 0 of a chunk, so the per-string-entry 'if (escaped)' test moves to a pre-loop 'if (escaped && n > 0) { escaped = false; i = 1; }'. PASS 576 cases. rel 1.033 (q1 0.905, q3 1.286). Sealed 1.631/1.643 vs base 1.605/1.640: within noise. One predictable branch per string is not a lever. Do not plan it.

ideas.title: STILL REJECTED from rounds 1-4 (do not resubmit)
ideas.evidence: Chunk-iteration reshaping (sync scanChunk 0.897, index-based array loop 0.882: ~16 chunks per build). Lazy recordEndLines (-5-10%) and Float64Array record offsets (-15-20%): the fixture has about 87.7k lines in 16 MB, so both pushes together cover under 1% of bytes. Per-line record push cost is not a lever. Buffer#indexOf quote/newline skipping: slower on ~26 B strings and wrong for raw newlines inside strings. Class table inside strings: slower than '> 0x5c'. nextCp counter: neutral three times. quoteFirst / quoteDirect peeling: neutral (V8 jump table). viewU8, skipDef, rej4n3: neutral (round 4). DataView SWAR and 2-word-per-step SWAR: negative (round 3). rej4u32 (lane-wise word reject) shares idea 1's slot, and its round-4 numbers came from the replace shape too. If it is ever used instead of idea 1, it must also replace rej4, but swarRG is the measured, better option. Remaining outside-string switch work (structural bytes, whitespace, newlines) is a small share after WCLS. This round found no outside-string change other than quoteInline worth more than 3%.
